instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

atoms.a: Personal responsibility has the biggest influence.

b.sound: The government needs to pass new laws. still, we all need to do our part in fighting against climate change. If we all take accountability for how we treat the environment, we can seriously change the way things are going, even though companies play a greater part in it.

Individuals changing their habits and taking on responsibility is great, but is it enough? It's the government that should enforce rules and regulations that the people and the firms who pay to make their own rules will actually stick to.

atoms.a: Those with the highest economic power make the rules.

b.sound: The government is really lacking at the moment. They could be doing so much more. Yet, I feel it's private jet owners and big companies who customize the rules and so I wonder if there is any use to an individual's partaking.

hint.label: Vocabulary

b.sound: I think of social media as this big My Friends book, like the one you had in primary school, where all your friends would write an entry, but even better. I enjoy seeing what everyone is up to these days, especially the friends that live abroad. It saves me from constantly needing to connect in real-life.

I adore that I can see my friend's pictures and what they're up to online. However, people are deceived by the anonymity and have completely forgotten social etiquette. Who is still able to hold a proper conversation nowadays? Such a shame!

atoms.a: Social media is prone to deception.

b.sound: Social networks used to be about connection. But when I open Instagram, all I see are fake people with fake lives, trying to sell me a product. We're being tricked to believe that we need to consume more in order to lead a fulfilling life, but none of that is true!

instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

atoms.a: Art needn't be taught as a subject.

b.sound: Art is one of the many graded subjects at school. Yet, Art isn't something to be taught, it should be experienced. It should be encouraged as an extracurricular activity, so that children get the chance to experience it without the pressure of educational attainment.

Art has always been subjective; and in order to stimulate creativity art should be encouraged in schools, but it should never be tied to a performance evaluation, that discourages creativity. I'm not sure whether it makes sense as a subject in this way.

atoms.a: Art is a subject like any other.

b.sound: In order to receive a well-rounded education, knowledge of the Arts is irreplaceable. I find the grading of art projects quite controversial. On the other hand, not everyone is great at science or languages either, so what's the difference?

instruction.text: Match each opinion with the corresponding speaker.

atoms.a: Car free cities increase accessibility inequality.

b.sound: Car-free cities seem utopian at first. I mean, the reduced noise and cleaner air. Amazing really. But it's so unfair for those who are not able-bodied and people who live on the outskirts of the city where public transport doesn't run every few minutes. Those who can't afford the high rent in the city would be even more disadvantaged.

atoms.a: Public spaces improve greatly due to car-free zones.

b.sound: I mean, just look at Paris. They did it right. Where there used to be so much traffic along the Seine, there are now beach chairs and paths, allowing new public space for the Parisians. Besides the improved air quality, this is where urban communities would really benefit.

atoms.a: Better air quality improves overall public health.

b.sound: We'd still have a long way to go in most cities because public transport would need to improve a lot to cater to everyone. But just think about all the fumes that come out of cars that pollute the air we breathe. If there were fewer cars, the air would be cleaner and people’s health would benefit in the long run.
